ican: I can describe the effects of friction in a drive system.
I can describe ways to reduce friction.
I can explain how to improve efficiency, with a cause and an effect.
I can calculate the efficiency of a system.

cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
Friction is a force that [[opposes|helps]] motion. In a drive system, friction wastes energy as [[heat|light]] and sound, and makes the moving parts [[wear|grow]].

To reduce friction, [[lubricate|paint]] the gears with oil or grease, fit [[bearings|springs]] on the shafts, or use a slippier material.

Efficiency = energy out ÷ energy [[in|lost]]. Efficiency has [[no unit|the unit J]]. No drive system is [[100%|0%]] efficient.

check.q: State two effects of friction in a gear train.
check.a: Any two: energy is lost as heat (and sound); the moving parts wear; the efficiency is lower.

check.q: State two ways to reduce friction in a gear train.
check.a: Any two: lubricate the gears (oil or grease); fit bearings; use a smoother ("slippier") material.

check.q: A motor gives 500 J of energy to a gear train. The gear train gives out 400 J. Calculate the efficiency.
Explain why lubricating the gears makes the battery of a cordless drill last longer.
check.a: Lubricating reduces friction (cause), so less energy is lost as heat and the battery lasts longer (effect).

check.q: Name the part fitted to a shaft to reduce friction.

paper2.alt: Pizzas are cooked as they move through an oven on a motorised conveyor: a drawing of the oven and conveyor. (e) Describe how friction in a mechanical system could be reduced. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2014 Question 16(e). Lubricate moving parts; use smoother materials where mechanisms interact; add bearings to the shaft. Any suitable description, saying what and where. No single word answers.

paper2.alt: The mechanical system in a self-balancing scooter: the motor at 4800 revs per minute turns gear A with 10 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 30 teeth. Gear C with 12 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D on the wheel, which turns at 200 revs per minute. (d) Explain how this mechanical system could be made more efficient. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2017 Question 12(d). Lubrication, bearings or a slippier material (cause, 1 mark) to reduce friction or energy loss to heat and sound (effect, 1 mark).

paper2.alt: A snow making machine in a container, and a free body diagram of the forces on its base. Ice is broken up by a cutter driven by a compound gear train: the motor at 1980 revs per minute turns gear A with 12 teeth, which meshes with gear B with 108 teeth. Gear C with 16 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D on the cutter, which turns at 55 revs per minute. (c) Explain how the efficiency of a compound gear train can be increased. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2021 Question 14(c). Lubricate, fit bearings or use a slippier material (cause, 1 mark) to reduce friction or energy loss to heat and sound (effect, 1 mark).

paper2.alt: A drill uses a 1.5 A, 18 V rated battery: a photograph of a cordless drill. Grease is used to lubricate the gear system within the drill. (b) Describe a reason for lubricating the gear system. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Question 6(b). Any one of: reduce wear on the gear system; the gears run smoother or quieter; improve efficiency or battery life; less heat, sound or energy losses. Accept reduces friction, or stops the gears rusting.

paper2.alt: 7. Friction can cause the moving parts of a drive system to wear out. (a) Describe how to reduce the wear on the moving parts of a drive system. 1 mark. (b) State a form of energy lost due to friction in a drive system. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2024 Question 7. (a) Any one of: regular maintenance; avoid overloading or revving; lubricate, oil or grease the parts. Do not accept single words. Accept the use of bearings or a slippery material. (b) Heat or sound energy.

paper2.alt: A photograph of an electric bike at a charging point, and its motor and gear train: gear A with 16 teeth meshes with gear B with 48 teeth; gear C with 16 teeth on the same shaft meshes with gear D with 64 teeth; the output turns at 120 revs per minute. (c) Explain how the efficiency of the gear train could be improved. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2024 Question 9(c). Lubricate or oil the gears (cause, with reference to the gear train, 1 mark) to reduce friction or energy loss (effect, 1 mark).

paper2.alt: A lifeboat winching system on a cruise ship: a photograph of lifeboats on the ship. A lifeboat of mass 7750 kg is lowered into the water. The lifeboat is winched back up to its starting position 15 m above the water level. (b) Calculate, showing all working and final unit: (i) the potential energy of the lifeboat, 2 marks; (ii) the efficiency of the system when the input energy to the winch is 2.50 MJ, 2 marks. (c) Explain why the winching system is not 100% efficient. 2 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2015 Question 11. (b)(i) Ep = mgh = 7750 x 9.8 x 15 = 1 139 250 J: 1 mark for substitution, 1 mark for the answer with unit. (b)(ii) Efficiency = Eout / Ein = 1.14 / 2.50 = 0.456 (0.46), or 45.6% (46%): 1 mark for substitution, 1 mark for the answer. Allow follow through from (b)(i). (c) Loss of energy as heat or sound (1 mark) due to friction (1 mark).

errors: No single words. "Oil" alone got no mark. Say what and where: lubricate the gears (2014, 2024).
"Explain" needs a cause and an effect: lubricate the gears (cause) to reduce friction, so less energy is lost (effect) (2017, 2021, 2024).
In 2024 the cause had to name the gear train: lubricate the gears, not just "lubricate".
Not 100% efficient: energy is lost as heat or sound (1 mark), due to friction (1 mark) (2015).
